_: THE PRICE LIST. Every number a customer pays lives in this file and nowhere else.
Not in a constant, not in a values file, not in a service. A price in code is a price that
needs a deploy to change, and a price that needs a deploy is one nobody changes — so the real
price list becomes a spreadsheet somebody keeps beside it, and the two disagree within a month.
ci/check_no_prices.py fails the build if a price appears in any Python we wrote.
AMOUNTS ARE IN HALALAS and include VAT, because that is what a Saudi customer is quoted: the
shop owner sees 148 and pays 148. amount 14800 is 148.00 SAR.
APPS ONLY, NOT A BASE AND APPS (2026-09-10) — الأساس RETIRED ENTIRELY
A ladder sells the wrong thing. A workshop that wants campaigns and will never look at an
association engine had to buy the engine to reach them, and read the difference between four
columns to find that out. Worse for us: every new thing we build has to be slotted into a
tier, which reprices three plans and re-argues the whole page. Invoicing and CRM are coming,
and the ladder has no room for them that does not disturb what is already sold.
A BUNDLED الأساس ROW WAS THE FIRST CUT AT THIS AND IT DID NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH THE
PRODUCT: it still smuggled a tier back in — every shop needed IT before any app meant anything
— and once every real capability (visit register, staff, branches, customer records) had its
own separately-priced app, the row sold nothing a shop could not already buy piece by piece.
Deleted outright (never a live subscriber to migrate — test server, never launched): the row,
its `feature.base` key, every write-gate that asked for it alone. Ordinary shop-management
writes (staff, branches, services) now accept ANY ONE paid app — see
services/operations/app/api/subscribed.py::subscribed_write's own comment for the OR.
MESSAGING/REMINDERS FOLLOWS THE SAME RULE, ONE LEVEL DOWN: it is not a plan row at all, it is
a FEATURE that comes bundled with whichever app actually records a customer event —
`feature.visit` or `feature.bookings` today. A shop owning either gets the reminders engine
(adaptive per-customer rhythm, engagement scoring) that ships with it; nothing here sells
'reminders' on its own, because there is nothing to remind about without an event to hang it
on. See services/reminders/app/api/subscribed.py::subscribed_write.
He pays for what he turned on, the page is a shop rather than a comparison table, and a new
app is a row here.
HOW IT ADDS UP, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW CODE. billing-service resolves entitlements across
EVERY live subscription and merges them — its own words: 'per-item catalogue — one
subscription per product — the union IS the entitlement'. Rich limits merge by combining
`limit`, and numbers SUM.
ONLY ONE ROW MAY EVER CARRY `messages.monthly` AT ONCE (the sentinel `unlimited`, never -1 —
billing merges its own sentinel by beating every arithmetic, and two -1s summed to -2, which
refuses every send). No row carries it today; the day unlimited messaging becomes its own sold
thing again, it goes on exactly one row and nowhere else.
AND AN APP IS NOT BOUGHT TWICE. Not expressible in billing — subscribe always creates a row —
so it is refused in our own path, operations' `subscription.activate`, which is the only door
the console uses. It decides from the SUBSCRIPTIONS THEMSELVES
(/internal/billing/subscriptions, base-services v0.16.7).
LIMITS ARE THE PRODUCT. The name sells; the limits dict is what actually happens. Three kinds,
and the difference decides who reports the number:
counter  consumed by whoever spends it, reset per period  — messages, custom templates
gauge    the CURRENT value of something owned elsewhere    — seats, branches
boolean  on or off                                          — the apps
AND 0 IS NOT ABSENCE. `0` means the key exists and the answer is DENY — which the console can
render as «هذا تطبيق لم تشترِه بعد، وهذا زر شرائه». A key missing everywhere means NOT
ENTITLED with no reason to show. So THE BASE CARRIES EVERY KEY, including the zeros, and every
shop therefore has an answer for every key whatever else it bought.
AND WE DO NOT SELL MESSAGES. The establishment contracts with Meta directly and Meta bills it
per delivered message, on a card in its own account — we neither buy them nor resell them, so
selling '1,000 a month' was selling what we do not own. Top-up packs went with it.
messages.monthly SURVIVES AS THE SENTINEL, and that is the whole point: unlimited still
counter in billing, so every send is measured and nothing is ever refused for a ceiling of
ours. It is a protection meter — it catches our own runaway loop before the owner's bill does
— and if we ever become a Solution Partner and messages are billed to us, a real number goes
back in this one field and the packs return unchanged.
His actual limit is what WhatsApp allows: 250 unique customers a day before verification,
2,000 after (spec 6.2.2). A second ceiling from us on top of theirs is a number he explains
twice and understands once.

Also GRANTS the reminders engine (adaptive rhythm, engagement scoring) as an included FEATURE, not a separate purchase — see services/reminders/app/api/subscribed.py::subscribed_write

Also GRANTS the reminders engine (adaptive rhythm, engagement scoring) as an included FEATURE, not a separate purchase — see services/reminders/app/api/subscribed.py::subscribed_write

_removed: feature.roles.custom IS GONE, and its absence is the honest state. It was sold on every tier
and the product has three fixed roles with no screen that creates a fourth — a line on an
invoice for something that does not exist. `ci/check_entitlements.py` found it the moment the
guard stopped counting a price-list LABEL as enforcement. It comes back the day it is built,
as its own app row, and nobody was charged for it in the meantime.

_: THE APPS. Each grants ONE key and says nothing about anything else — a row that repeated
`staff.seats` would add its number to the base's every time somebody bought it.
ONE PRICE FOR EVERY APP — 99. The first cut derived four different prices from the old
ladder, and the ladder is exactly what we stopped selling: a shop comparing 60 against
200 is reading a tier list again, and asking us to justify why one app costs three of
another.
One number ends that conversation. He reads the sentence about what an app DOES and says
yes or no — which is the decision we want him making, and the only one he can make fast.
AND IT IS EASIER TO SELL THAN TO PRICE. «كل تطبيق بـ99» is repeatable by a partner on a
phone call; four numbers are a page somebody has to open.

_: REQUIRES_ANY (2026-09-09), THE OWNER'S OWN REASONING: points earned on nothing are not a
programme, they are a promise with no way to keep it. Loyalty points are earned by a
customer TOUCHPOINT — a visit recorded, or an appointment attended — and a shop holding
NEITHER تسجيل زيارة nor الحجوزات has no way for a single point to ever be earned.
`plan.requires_any` says so, data-driven,
exactly like `plan.standalone` above: `may_add` (services/operations/app/core/

intersect this list — independent of, and in addition to, the ordinary base-required
rule. A THIRD app may declare its own dependency the same way, with one edit here and
zero code changes.

just this and connect its own WhatsApp number. `plan.standalone` is the marker

rule for THIS plan only — every other app row still needs الأساس first, unchanged. Shaped
as an ordinary boolean limit (not under the `feature.` prefix, so it grants nothing and
`ci/check_entitlements.py` never treats it as a sold capability) so billing merges it the
same well-tested way it merges every other boolean flag.
199, THE OWNER'S OWN PRICE (2026-09-06) — high enough to bundle a real included usage
allowance with it rather than selling bare access; see the `credits` note below.
NAMED FOR WHAT IT DOES, NOT FOR THE CHANNEL — the owner's own decision: the plan's NAME
never says WhatsApp, and DOES say 'bot'/'smart' (an AI capability is the whole sell). The

LIMIT_WORDS['feature.whatsapp'] on the pricing page (apps/console/src/screens/Plans.tsx) —

OPERATIONS STILL NEEDS A SHOP RECORD to attach a WhatsApp number to (a branch to register
the sending identity against) — signup itself is unconditional today, so a standalone
buyer already has one before he ever reaches this plan.
STANDALONE_PLANS_ENABLED (operations/app/config.py) is the kill switch: false makes
`may_add` demand الأساس for this row too, same as every other app, without unlisting or
deleting it — existing standalone subscribers are unaffected, only new purchases stop.
INCLUDED ALLOWANCE = A PERCENT OF THIS PLAN'S OWN PRICE, LIVE-EDITABLE, NO REDEPLOY —
the owner's own call (2026-09-11): a fixed halala amount was tried first (the full price,
19900) and rejected — «بكرة نبغ المضمنة تكون 20%، قرار بيدنا». `credit_percent_of_price`
below OPTS THIS PLAN IN to billing-service's percent-of-price grant (v0.19.20); the actual

key=PLAN_CREDIT_PERCENT, tenant='' (platform scope) — never edited here, never a reseed.
Computed off the LIST price at grant time (a coupon/discount-rule never shrinks it);
percent 0 grants nothing — the feature stays off until an operator sets one.

_: جهات الاتصال — THE ONE FREE APP ON THE PRICE LIST, and deliberately so: the owner's own
decision was that registering a customer must be possible «من أي تطبيق», and a shop with
no other product at all must still be able to open the one door that resolves-or-creates a
customer by phone (POST /field/customers/ensure). A price on that door would put the
product's front door behind a paywall nobody else on the price list has to clear first.
amount: 0, ON PURPOSE. billing-service takes the charge at renewal, not at subscribe — see
`_charge_invoice`'s own zero-total branch, which already auto-succeeds a 0-halala invoice
with no gateway call — so a free row needs no special handling there. What DOES need one
is our own `may_subscribe` (services/operations/app/core/subscribe.py), which used to
refuse ANY subscribe with no `payment_token` regardless of price; it now treats a plan
whose resolved price is 0 as paid whether or not a token was sent.
SUBSCRIBED WITH interval='once', NOT 'month' — services/operations/app/api/v1/
subscription.py forces this for every free row, this one included: `once` sets
`period_end` to 0, which the resolver reads as 'never lapses' and the renewal sweep skips
outright, so a free-forever app never re-cycles through a pointless SAR 0 invoice every
month for nothing.
`plan.standalone` — same marker, same reason as «بوت خدمة العملاء الذكي» above: nothing
in this product requires any OTHER app first any more, but the marker still exists for
`may_add`'s own OR-across-every-app rule; `STANDALONE_PLANS_ENABLED` is the same kill
switch for every row that carries it.
`feature.contacts` GRANTS NOTHING BEYOND THE ONE DOOR IT NAMES — it is read by
`subscribed_write_or_customer_creating_app` (services/operations/app/api/subscribed.py)
alongside `feature.bookings`; it does not touch visits, which stay behind `feature.visit`
(see «تسجيل زيارة» below) even for a customer this app just created.

bundled with a tier, so a two-branch shop that wanted nothing else had to buy الذكية to
get a second branch.
ONE SEAT PER UNIT, NOT A PACK OF TEN. This row used to grant 10 seats per purchase (named
«10 مقاعد إضافية») on the theory that a repeated purchase was the simpler story to tell an
owner. It was overtaken by the console's own capacity UI (Plans.tsx's CapacityAddonCard,
«السعة» section): a single +/- stepper that moves one subscription's own `quantity` up and
down, never a second row and never a repeated purchase — so the unit this file must grant
IS the unit the stepper adds one of at a time. Left at 10 the stepper's own «1» press
silently bought ten, and the live plan was hand-corrected on the server to grant 1 well
before this file caught up — which is exactly the drift seed-plans.sh exists to close,
and precisely the drift THIS row still carried until now.
THE PRICE IS STILL THE ONLY ONE NOT DERIVED FROM THE OLD LADDER — a starting point, meant
to be argued with; editing this file is the whole mechanism.
